subject: Private DNS origination and egress-proxy plan for tenant subdomains
messages:
From: John Rogers <jrogers@acmehealth.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Private dns mapping for tenant *.acme.internal + TLS termination question

Hi Aisha / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We are moving toward a pilot of Redwood Private in our VPC and need to align on how tenant hostnames will be resolved and how TLS termination should be handled across our environment. High level asks: 
- We will own the apex acme.internal in our VPC. How should we delegate or assert ownership for subdomains like tenant1.acme.internal vs the proxy endpoints Redwood will accept?
- We need to understand certificate sources: can we use our internal PKI (HSM-backed) or should we run ACME against an internal ACME responder?
- For egress/proxying: we need guidance on whether Redwood should terminate TLS at the customer edge and re-initiate outbound connections, or if we should use a mutual-TLS bridging model.

Attached a quick scan from our security team showing current certificate inventory (acme-cert-scan-results.zip). Can you propose an ops-friendly approach that minimizes cross-team handoffs? Also please flag anything that will require procurement/legal changes.

Thanks,
John
John Rogers
Head of Platform Security, Acme Health

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: John Rogers <jrogers@acmehealth.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-13T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private dns mapping for tenant *.acme.internal + TLS termination question

John — thanks for the details and the scan. Quick summary of the approach I recommend below; Jordan added the deeper ops steps in a follow-up.

Proposal (summary):
- DNS origination: Keep acme.internal authoritative in your VPC. For Redwood Private endpoints we recommend a short CNAME delegation pattern: provider endpoints under rw-prv-eu1.redwood-internal.net (internal-only) and you create CNAMEs from tenantX.acme.internal -> tenantX.rw-prv-eu1.redwood-internal.net. This preserves ownership while allowing us to rotate endpoint IPs.
- TLS source options: three supported modes: 1) Customer-managed CA certs (you push cert+key material to a secure vault we consume via encrypted transfer), 2) Internal ACME responder where we perform DNS or HTTP-01 proof inside your VPC to issue per-host certs, 3) Redwood-managed certs (least operational burden). For regulated data you will likely choose option 1.
- Termination model: We support two patterns: A) termination at customer edge with mutual TLS between your edge and Redwood runtime (recommended for strict egress control), or B) termination at a Redwood edge inside the VPC + re-encrypt to upstream (recommended when you want simpler SNI mapping). Mutual TLS (A) requires client cert provisioning and periodic rotation; B requires control-plane proof-of-possession for certs.

Operational notes:
- Rotation: If you manage certs, we accept PKCS#12 or PEM bundles uploaded to a vault endpoint; we support scheduled automatic rotation with an upload endpoint and a webhook to confirm successful swap.
- DNS proof: If you run an ACME responder inside the VPC, we can call it directly; otherwise we do DNS TXT proofs against acme.internal if your DNS team is comfortable creating short-lived TXT records.

I'm attaching a short decision memo that compares the tradeoffs (acme-ca-options-summary.pdf). Propose a sync tomorrow to pick a mode and list exact personnel for cert handoffs.

— Aisha
Aisha Rahman
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: John Rogers <jrogers@acmehealth.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-13T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private dns mapping for tenant *.acme.internal + TLS termination question

John / Aisha — adding implementation details so your ops/security teams can evaluate. TL;DR: we prefer the CNAME-origin pattern + either customer-managed certs (push) or internal ACME responder for per-tenant certs.

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Zone proof and CNAMEs
   - You keep acme.internal as authoritative. Create a short-lived delegation record set that points tenantX.acme.internal to tenantX.rw-prv-us1.redwood.local (CNAME). We supply the target names once the staging runtime is provisioned.
2) SNI / Host verification
   - Redwood runtime validates the presented cert's SAN against the requested SNI. If customer-managed certs are used, the runtime will accept the cert from the customer vault and bind it to the endpoint.
3) Mutual TLS option (edge-termination):
   - Your edge will terminate incoming client connections. Then the edge establishes a mutual TLS session to the Redwood runtime using a client cert we trust. We rotate trust anchors via a monthly cadence; we can push CRLs/OCSP stapling to your OCSP responder if you require immediate revocation checks.
4) Egress and upstream connections:
   - When Redwood needs to reach back to external services, we recommend you provide an egress proxy with an allowlist. If you require full control, we can run a tiny egress sidecar that tunnels traffic through your proxy.
5) Audit & logging:
   - We will emit per-connection audit events (SNI, cert thumbprint) to your SIEM endpoint; we need an ingestion endpoint (syslog/HTTPS).

Caveats & dependencies:
- If you pick push-managed certs, legal will likely request an updated hosting addendum.
- ACME-internal requires a reachable responder in the VPC that follows the Redwood ACME client expectations (we'll share a small container image).

Next steps: 1) Confirm which cert mode you prefer, 2) identify your DNS owner + cert owner, 3) schedule a 60-min ops handoff.

On a separate note, I included a brief checklist (mutual-tls-checklist.xlsx) with the exact fields we need when you push certs.

— Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team: 
- For the CNAME approach, are we introducing any MITM risk if the CNAME is visible in any logs? We need to be explicit for our auditors.
- For client cert rotation: can Redwood support key material that never leaves our HSM (i.e., Redwood holds only cert references and performs operations through an HSM-backed signing proxy)?

We attached the cert inventory in case it helps (acme-cert-scan-results.zip). Goal is to avoid wholesale CA imports if possible.

John

John — looping in procurement/contracting next steps so we can keep the pilot timeline. A few practical items: 
- If Acme chooses push-managed certs and we need to store customer certs/keys in our vault, this typically triggers the Private deployment Addendum. We can surface a one-page amendment for legal review quickly.
- If you pick the ACME-internal model, there is no key escrow/transfer which is attractive for security teams — fewer contractual changes.
- For pricing: mutual-TLS edge termination (where we run persistent mTLS sessions per tenant) is slightly higher due to stateful footprint; we can provide a pilot quote.

Please confirm preferred cert mode and I will route the right paperwork and assign a technical project manager to coordinate the ops handoff.

— Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
